findings.title: New abstract `order()` method breaks external CryptoProvider implementations
findings.body: `int order();` is added as an abstract method to the public `CryptoProvider` interface. Any third-party or downstream implementation (e.g. in the keycloak-client repo, adapters, custom FIPS providers) will fail to compile and will throw `AbstractMethodError` at runtime when loaded via ServiceLoader. Give it a `default` implementation (e.g. `return 100;` or 0) to keep the interface backward compatible.

findings.title: Ambiguous provider selection no longer fails fast and is logged only at debug
findings.body: Previously having multiple `CryptoProvider`s on the classpath threw `IllegalStateException`. Now the highest `order()` wins, but `DefaultCryptoProvider`, `FIPS1402Provider` and `WildFlyElytronProvider` all return 200, so if two of them are on the classpath (a real misconfiguration, e.g. default + fips) the choice is arbitrary/ServiceLoader-order dependent and silently proceeds, only noted via `debug` logging. Consider distinct orders and/or a warn-level message when two providers share the top order.

findings.title: logger.debugf called with a dynamic string as format
findings.body: `logger.debugf(builder.toString())` passes a runtime-built string as the format template. If any class name or future content contains a '%' character this throws/misformats (java.util.IllegalFormatException). Use `logger.debugf("Ignored crypto providers: %s", ...)` with the value as an argument.

findings.title: getKeyStore uses enum name() instead of toString() unlike other providers
findings.body: All other CryptoProvider implementations call `KeyStore.getInstance(format.toString())`. `KeystoreFormat` overrides `toString()` (the JCA type string may differ from the enum constant name, e.g. for PKCS12/BCFKS variants), so using `format.name()` here can request a nonexistent keystore type and make `getSupportedKeyStoreTypes()` report wrong results. Use `format.toString()` for consistency.

findings.title: Indefinite-length sequence silently decodes as empty list
findings.body: `readLength()` returns -1 for indefinite-length encoding (0x80). In `readSequence()` the loop `while (length > 0)` is then never entered, so an indefinite-length SEQUENCE returns an empty list instead of an error, and callers then throw a confusing "Invalid sequence with size different to 2" or mis-handle it. Reject length < 0 explicitly in readSequence/readInteger.

findings.title: Dead ASN1Encoder.create().write(...) calls
findings.body: Lines 114-115 create two ASN1Encoder instances, write the integers and discard the results; they have no effect since the DER sequence is built on lines 117-121. Remove them to avoid confusion (and wasted allocations).

findings.title: Test only round-trips its own encoder and uses a wrong-size key for ES384/ES512
findings.body: The key pair is generated with the JDK default EC curve (typically P-256) yet the test runs with `ECDSAAlgorithm.ES384`/`ES512` signature lengths, so the signatures are not representative of those algorithms. Additionally the assertion only compares the decoder's output with itself after re-encoding, so a systematically incorrect DER encoding (e.g. missing padding or wrong tags) would still pass. The test should use the proper curve per algorithm and verify interoperability, e.g. compare against the BouncyCastle-based `BCECDSACryptoProvider` output and/or verify the re-encoded DER with `Signature.verify()`.
